what_its_for: Casimersen is used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a change (mutation) in the DMD gene that can be treated by skipping exon 45. It helps your body make a shorter but still working form of a protein called dystrophin, which your muscles need to stay strong. It does not cure DMD, but it may help slow the loss of muscle function.
how_to_take: Casimersen is given as an infusion (drip) directly into your vein (IV) by a healthcare provider, usually at a clinic or infusion center. Each infusion takes about 35 to 60 minutes. You will receive it once a week, every week. Do not try to give this medicine to yourself at home unless your doctor has specifically trained you and approved it.
dosing: The usual dose is 30 mg for every kilogram (kg) of your body weight, given once a week by IV infusion. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your weight. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled infusion, contact your doctor or healthcare provider as soon as possible to reschedule. Try to get back on your regular weekly schedule. Do not try to make up for a missed dose by taking two doses at the same time or in the same week.
storage: Casimersen is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or infusion center. If you are given vials to take home, store them in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep the vials in their original box to protect them from light. Do not freeze. If stored at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C), use within 14 days. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods, drinks, or activities you must strictly avoid while taking casimersen. However, always tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, since some may interact with this drug. Stay up to date with all your follow-up appointments and lab tests, since your doctor needs to monitor your kidney function regularly.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, or feeling faint during or after the infusion; signs of a kidney problem such as less urination than usual, swelling in your legs or feet, or feeling very tired; pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site; or any new or worsening symptoms. Also call your doctor if you have a fever, chills, or feel unusually unwell after an infusion.
when_it_works: Casimersen works gradually over time. Some patients may begin to show increased dystrophin levels in their muscles within a few months, but it may take longer to notice any changes in muscle strength or function. It is important to keep taking this medicine regularly as prescribed, even if you do not feel different right away. Talk to your doctor about what results to expect and when.
special_populations: Children and Teenagers: Casimersen has been studied in pediatric patients with DMD and is approved for use in children. Doses are based on body weight. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems, as this may affect how your body handles the medicine and whether dose changes are needed. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if casimersen is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medicine.
